disposition.reason: A neighbor appealed the St. Albans ZBA's decision on an application for a right-of-way extension whose stated purpose is to serve a new two-lot subdivision for two single-family dwellings; the court decided that application. The subdivision approval itself was held not to be before the court, so housing rests on the access permit being permission for new house lots.

judgments.note: Municipal appeal is clear. Housing is yes because the application is a right-of-way extension whose stated purpose is to serve a new two-lot subdivision for two single-family dwellings (new house lots); but the court says the subdivision approval itself is not before it, so a reader could treat this as access/road work only.
See disposition: the permit at issue is access for two new house lots, not the subdivision approval itself.

The words 'de novo' do not appear, but the court held an evidentiary hearing, made its own findings without having the ZBA decision, and itself denied the application; no on-the-record procedure is mentioned.
No filing date is stated; start is bounded only by the May 12, 2003 decision, which is also the end, so the zero-day minimum is unknown.
The ZBA decision was not provided to the court and its outcome is never stated; a neighbor's appeal suggests approval but this is not established.

Coleman is the neighbor appellant and represented herself. seeks=overturn_approval is inferred from her opposing the application (her engineer's testimony against it) and appealing; the ZBA outcome itself is not stated.
The court states the right-of-way will only serve two single-family dwellings on the two proposed lots; counted as 2, though the subdivision itself was not before the court.
The parcel is to be divided into two new lots (2.6 and 1.2 acres) with no existing housing; subdivision approval not before the court.
Contentions concern well isolation distance (fixed state rule) and runoff affecting her well; the municipal standard applied to runoff is not stated, so unknown.

questions: Should a right-of-way/access approval whose sole stated purpose is to serve a proposed two-lot residential subdivision count as new housing when the court says the subdivision approval itself is not before it?
